text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The ministerial committee on privatisation, at a meeting yesterday under Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri, approved the privatisation programme for the first half of this year, which includes measures to prepare 30 companies for sale. Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid said it was decided to offer new tranches of shares in nine companies so that the private sector would own more than 51 percent of them. These companies are Misr Chemical Industries, Paints and Chemical Industries/PACHIN, Heliopolis Housing and Development, United Arab Spinning and Weaving/Unirab, Alexandria Spinning and Weaving/Spinalex, Kabo/Nasr Clothing and Textiles, Extracted Oils and Derivatives, Eastern Company and Nile Pharmaceuticals and Chemical Industries.
The committee also decided to continue to offer shares in 20 companies which have already been partially privatised, in such a way that the private-sector stake would rise to 90 percent.
Obeid also said that within a week ministries must submit their plans for selling off the public-sector stake in joint ventures such as banks and insurance companies.
-- Obeid said the government had no intention of imposing new taxes on equities and the general trend is to alleviate burdens and to offer other advantages to attract investment.
-- President Hosni Mubarak had preliminary talks with Gambian President Yahya Jammeh after he arrived yesterday afternoon.

-- Mubarak will arrive in the Swiss town of Davos on Friday to take part in the World Economic Forum. He will speak at the closing session on Sunday, which will be devoted to the Middle East and North Africa.
-- The police thwarted an attempt to smuggle in automatic weapons and ammunition from Sudan. Fifteen Egyptians and Sudanese took part in the attempt.

- The Shoura Council condemned deviation by the "Satanists" from the traditions of Egyptian society, which observes worship of the one and only God. Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif told the council that that the Egyptian media are trying to protect society from a foreign cultural invasion.
- At the Davos meeting Mubarak will explained Egypt's economic experience, the political situation in the Middle East and the possibilities for regional cooperation.

- The Mufti, Nasr Farid Wassil said in Tanta that the Satanists are apostates but should be given a chance to repent because they are young. If they abandon their corrupt ideas, they can be forgiven but if they persist in their error they should face the penalty prescribed by Islamic law.
-- 108 people suffered asphyxiation and poisoning in an explosion of ammonia gas in a factory in Alexandria. Eight of the people are in serious cases.
- Standard rules for voluntary early retirement at public-sector companies are being prepared and will be announced before Eid al-Fitr (about February 9).
